# 07 · Products: staff can rename a product

**Type:** Test coverage · **Area:** Catalogue / Products · **Priority:** Medium

## Context

Merchandisers rename products all the time (a season name, a spelling fix). The name is edited on
the product page and saved with the page's Save button; the page title follows the name. We have
no e2e coverage of the product page, and a rename that silently does not save is exactly the kind
of failure nobody notices until a customer does.

## What to cover

1. Open **E2E Hoodie** from the orders test data.
2. Change its name to "E2E Zip Hoodie" and save.
3. The product carries the new name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After saving, the page title shows "E2E Zip Hoodie".
- [ ] After a reload, the name field and the page title both show "E2E Zip Hoodie".

## Notes

- Use the existing orders test data; the product is already there.

1	# 07 · Products: staff can rename a product
2	
3	**Type:** Test coverage · **Area:** Catalogue / Products · **Priority:** Medium
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Merchandisers rename products all the time (a season name, a spelling fix). The name is edited on
8	the product page and saved with the page's Save button; the page title follows the name. We have
9	no e2e coverage of the product page, and a rename that silently does not save is exactly the kind
10	of failure nobody notices until a customer does.
11	
12	## What to cover
13	
14	1. Open **E2E Hoodie** from the orders test data.
15	2. Change its name to "E2E Zip Hoodie" and save.
16	3. The product carries the new name.
17	
18	## Acceptance criteria
19	
20	- [ ] After saving, the page title shows "E2E Zip Hoodie".
21	- [ ] After a reload, the name field and the page title both show "E2E Zip Hoodie".
22

1	# E2E against a local Saleor
2	
3	A disposable Saleor in docker, the dashboard built from your working tree, and a database
4	restored to a known state before every test. No Saleor Cloud, no shared snapshot, no
5	hand-maintained fixture ids.
6	
7	```bash
8	pnpm e2e            # the stable target (latest 3.23 patch)
9	pnpm e2e:main       # Saleor's unreleased main branch
10	pnpm e2e:all        # both, one after the other
11	pnpm e2e --ui       # ...and anything else Playwright understands
12	pnpm e2e:fresh      # drop the database volume and the caches first
13	pnpm e2e:down       # stop both stacks, keep the volumes
14	```
15	
16	To test feedback against the real PostHog SDK in the production dashboard build:
17	
18	```bash
19	IS_CLOUD_INSTANCE=true POSTHOG_HOST=https://posthog.example.test \
20	POSTHOG_KEY=phc_feedback_e2e POSTHOG_EXCLUDED_DOMAINS= \
21	pnpm e2e tests/feedback.spec.ts
22	```
23	
24	This uses the existing analytics configuration at an intercepted test endpoint. The specs
25	serve the installed survey script and production-shaped survey responses, including the trigger selector
26	condition, and cover loading, opening/submitting feedback, blocked requests, and no
27	matching survey. No analytics or feedback is sent to PostHog.
28	
29	A first run pulls the image, migrates, seeds and builds the dashboard: about **2.5 minutes**
30	before the first test. A warm run reaches it in **13 seconds**. Every phase announces itself
31	with its elapsed time (`[e2e 1m59s] > running populatedb`), so a slow run is visibly a slow
32	run rather than a hang.
33	
34	Measured on an M-series laptop: baseline migration 1m16s and `populatedb` 20s (both once per
35	Saleor image), the dump 0.4 MB, and **1.5-2.5s to restore it before each test**.
36	
37	## The two targets
38	
39	The dashboard supports two API generations at once: the latest stable Saleor and the
40	unreleased main branch. Which one a build speaks to is decided by `FF_USE_STAGING_SCHEMA`,
41	and that flag is **build-time** — it reaches the bundle through vite's `define`
42	(`vite.config.js`), which decides which generated GraphQL tree survives tree-shaking. There
43	is no runtime switch, so a target is a Saleor image _and_ a dashboard build.
44	
45	| Target   | Image                                 | Schema  | API  | Dashboard |
46	| -------- | ------------------------------------- | ------- | ---- | --------- |
47	| `stable` | `ghcr.io/saleor/saleor:3.23`          | main    | 8200 | 9200      |
48	| `main`   | `ghcr.io/saleor/saleor:unstable-main` | staging | 8300 | 9300      |
49	
50	`3.23` is floating on purpose, and the suite re-resolves both tags itself before starting
51	anything (`pullImage`): a Saleor patch release is picked up by the next run rather than by a
52	version-bump PR. When 3.24 ships, `config.ts` is the one file to edit — stable becomes
53	`3.24`, and main keeps tracking whatever is unreleased.
54	
55	The ports differ per target so a stack left running from the other one cannot answer by
56	accident, and the two compose projects keep their containers and volumes apart.
57	
58	## What a run does
59	
60	1. **Builds the dashboard** into `build-e2e-<target>/`, skipped when nothing it is built
61	   from has changed. Kept out of `build/` so a running `pnpm dev` is unaffected.
62	2. **Brings the stack up** — Postgres, Valkey, Saleor api + worker, and an nginx serving
63	   that build through the repository's own `nginx/default.conf`.
64	3. **Ensures the seed** for the scenario (below), building it if this Saleor image has not
65	   produced one yet.
66	4. **Signs every actor in** over the API, caching one `localStorage` entry per actor.
67	5. **Restores the database before every test.**
68	
69	## Seeds are built, not written
70	
71	A scenario is a named database state. It is _built_ once per Saleor image — slowly, through
72	`populatedb` and the GraphQL API — and captured as a `pg_dump --data-only`. Tests never run
73	a build; they restore the dump, which is a truncate and a `COPY`.
74	
75	The base scenario is Saleor's own `populatedb`: 32 products, two channels, categories,
76	collections, pages, menus, vouchers, gift cards, orders, customers, promotions, shipping
77	zones, warehouses, tax classes — and one staff user per permission, which is what the suite
78	signs in as. It is used instead of a bootstrap of our own because Saleor core maintains it,
79	so it follows schema changes for free.
80	
81	**Dumps are cached under the Saleor image's content id.** A new `3.23` patch or a fresh
82	`unstable-main` finds no cache and rebuilds, which is what makes following a floating tag
83	safe. Cached logins share the key, so a rebuilt seed can never be paired with a token minted
84	against the users it replaced.
85	
86	Write scenario builds against the **GraphQL API**. Raw SQL is the escape hatch for states
87	the API cannot express (a row shaped by an older migration, a stock no mutation leaves
88	behind) — the dump captures both identically, but SQL is the part that rots when Saleor's
89	tables change, and this suite deliberately tracks a moving image.
90	
91	To add one: a file in `scenarios/`, registered in `scenarios/registry.ts`, and
92	`test.use({ scenario: "..." })` in the spec. A scenario builds from an empty database, or -
93	with `parent: "default"` - on top of another scenario's dump. Build on `default` unless you
94	need to replace it: a second `populatedb` mints different staff rows, and the cached sessions
95	only work against the rows they were signed in with.
96	
97	The stack runs a Celery worker but **no beat**, and Saleor leaves some work to beat alone -
98	new products are not searchable, and catalogue promotions do not reach prices, until a
99	periodic task runs. `ensureScenario` therefore runs those tasks after every build, before the
100	dump (`lib/beat.ts`). A scenario that creates something another beat task settles adds that
101	task there.
102	
103	## Isolation, and opting into parallel
104	
105	By default the database is restored **before every test**, and those tests run one at a
106	time. That single property is what the suite is for: a failing test reproduces on its own,
107	rather than as a function of the tests that ran before it. Specs need no cleanup
108	discipline and no unique names, and nothing in the seed is ever consumed.
109	
110	Serial is the default because a restore empties every table for a second or two — a test
111	running alongside one would see a shop with no products and no users in it.
112	
113	A block that leaves nothing behind can opt out of the reset, and then run in parallel:
114	
115	```ts
116	import { parallel } from "../config.ts";
117	
118	test.describe("Catalogue list", { tag: parallel() }, () => { ... });      // default scenario
119	test.describe("Refunds", { tag: parallel("refunded-orders") }, () => { ... });
120	```
121	
122	The tag takes a **scenario name**, so the group and the database state it runs on are the
123	same thing and cannot drift apart. A run is then:
124	
125	```
126	restore:default          one restore, alone
127	parallel:default         every test tagged parallel(),          all at once
128	restore:refunded-orders  one restore, alone
129	parallel:refunded-orders every test tagged parallel("refunded-orders"), all at once
130	stable                   everything untagged, one at a time, each from its own reset
131	```
132	
133	Groups run one after another and all of them before the serial phase, rather than
134	interleaved in declaration order. That is deliberate, and it is also the cheaper
135	arrangement: this costs one restore per group plus one per serial test, where interleaving
136	would add a restore at every boundary and buy nothing — tests are independent by
137	construction, so the order between groups carries no meaning.
138	
139	Playwright's project `dependencies` are what enforce it; they are the only ordering
140	primitive that spans workers, which is also why a group's restore is a project rather than
141	a hook. A scenario with no tagged tests still pays for its restore project (a second or
142	two) — whether a group has members is not knowable when the config is read.
143	
144	`E2E_WORKERS` (default 4) sets how wide the parallel phase runs. Each test is a browser
145	context, so the ceiling is memory rather than cores.
146	
147	Because arrangement cannot be done as an admin at test time, **a state a spec needs is a
148	scenario**, named and built, not something the spec creates on the way past.
149	
150	### What cannot be tagged: signing in
151	
152	Saleor blocks an IP for a second before _every_ login attempt — deliberately, "to prevent
153	concurrent requests" (`saleor/account/throttling.py`), unconditionally in `tokenCreate`,
154	with no setting to disable it. Every test here comes from the same address, so parallel
155	UI logins mostly fail with `LOGIN_ATTEMPT_DELAYED`. `tests/login.spec.ts` therefore stays
156	in the serial phase.
157	
158	Specs that arrive **already signed in** are unaffected: a stored session refreshes its
159	token, and nothing throttles that. Those are the ones worth tagging.
160	
161	There is no setting for it. `authenticate_with_throttling` is called unconditionally from
162	`CreateToken.get_user` (`saleor/graphql/account/mutations/authentication/create_token.py:53`),
163	nothing in `settings.py` guards it, and the delays are module constants rather than settings
164	(`MIN_DELAY`/`MAX_DELAY` in `saleor/account/throttling.py:14-16`). The image exposes no env
165	var to turn it off.
166	
167	What it does use is the default Django cache (`throttling.py:5`), which Saleor builds from
168	`CACHE_URL` (`settings.py:987-992`). Pointing that at a dummy backend therefore removes the
169	block — `cache.add` always succeeds and stores nothing — so `SALEOR_CACHE_URL=dummy://` makes
170	the login spec pass 15-wide in 35s rather than 1.2m. It is offered as a lever, not a default,
171	because it disables Saleor's cache _everywhere_ — app dataloaders, the webhook circuit
172	breaker, observability — and a suite whose Saleor is configured unlike production can
173	mislead about exactly the features that depend on those.
174	
175	## Actors
176	
177	`test.use({ actor: "order" })` signs the whole spec in as
178	`order.manager@example.com` — one of the single-permission staff users `populatedb` mints
179	(`create_staffs` in Saleor's `saleor/core/utils/random_data.py`), which is what makes
180	missing-permission flows testable. `admin` is the superuser; `anonymous` carries no session,
181	for specs that sign in through the UI themselves. A scenario that seeds its own staff member
182	can name it by email.
183	
184	## Porting from `e2e-legacy/`
185	
186	`e2e-legacy/` is the Cloud-snapshot suite. **It is frozen — do not edit it.** Its results
187	cannot be observed without provisioning a Cloud instance, so a change there is a change
188	nobody can verify.
189	
190	Port by copying: bring the page objects a spec needs into `pages/`, reviewing them on the
191	way in. The locators are `data-test-id`s and carry over unchanged; what does not carry is
192	`@data/e2eTestData`, the 780 lines of snapshot ids. Point the spec at the seed instead, or
193	at a scenario built for it.
194	
195	Locators become `readonly` class fields initialized from `this.page`, with an empty
196	`constructor(readonly page: Page) {}` - not the legacy defaulted constructor parameters. The
197	constructor then takes only what a caller injects, so nothing reads as overridable when it
198	is not. (`useDefineForClassFields: false` in `tsconfig.json` is what lets the fields see
199	`this.page`.)
200	
201	## Deferred
202	
203	Real shortcuts, taken knowingly, with what would undo them:
204	
205	- **The serial phase is serial.** One database per worker (`saleor_w0`, `saleor_w1`, …)
206	  restored from the same dump would parallelise the resetting tests too. Do it when serial
207	  run time, not the reseed itself, is what hurts — note it also needs one Saleor API per
208	  database, and the dashboard bundle bakes its `API_URL` at build time.
209	- **Reset per test.** Batch to per-file for specs that demonstrably do not need it — but
210	  only against a measurement, since it trades back the reproducibility above.
211	- **No parallel group has members yet.** `tests/login.spec.ts` cannot be tagged (above).
212	  The first ported spec that reads without writing should be.
213	- **Only the superuser signs in through the UI.** The flow is shared code for every user,
214	  so the other actors are covered by global setup signing them in over the API.

217	  fingerprint, or a shared build cache in CI, would cut a cold run substantially.
218	- **`nginx/replace-env-vars.sh` is not exercised.** The bundle is mounted read-only and its
219	  environment is baked at build time (it has to be, for the schema flag). The shipped
220	  image's runtime substitution therefore has no coverage here; it wants a smoke test of the
221	  actual Docker image, which is a different suite.

223	  failed nightly run posts its failed tests to Slack; a manual run does not.
224	  Putting it on pull requests is a one-line change once the suite is broad enough to be
225	  worth the minutes.

input.overview:

## Setup, following CLAUDE.md "E2E conventions" and e2e/README.md

- Spec file: e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts. It opens with a comment saying what it covers and why: there is no product-page coverage yet, and a rename that silently fails to save is the kind of failure nobody notices.
- Import test and expect from "../../fixtures/test.ts", never from @playwright/test. Relative imports keep the .ts extension.
- Use test.use({ scenario: ORDERS_SCENARIO }). ORDERS_SCENARIO and PRODUCTS are imported from "../../scenarios/orders.ts". The original name is PRODUCTS.hoodie.name ("E2E Hoodie"). The new name is a spec constant: const NEW_NAME = "E2E Zip Hoodie".

- No new scenario, no API set-up, no beforeEach or afterEach, no cleanup, no unique or timestamped names. The fixture restores the database before every test. Do not tag the test parallel(), because it writes.
- No hard-coded product ids, since ids change with every dump build. The test reaches the product through the UI by name (see "Reaching the product" below).
- Title is a sentence ending in the #e2e tag, for example "staff can rename a product and the new name persists #e2e". An area tag such as #products may follow it.
- One test with three test.step stages: "open the product", "rename and save", "reload and verify". Mark the set-up with // Arrange. Mark the steps // Act & Assert, because acting and asserting alternate stage by stage.
- No waitForTimeout and no networkidle. Do not change retries or timeouts. Assertions are web-first, for example await expect(locator).toHaveValue(...).

## Reaching the product (no stable id)

The Products list (/products) is a Glide data grid drawn on a canvas. Its rows are not real DOM rows or links, and the only way into them is the legacy fiber hack (clickGridCell in e2e-legacy/pages/basePage.ts). Do not use it. The tile view (tile-view-button) does have DOM tiles, but each tile's test id contains the product id (product-tile-<id>), and the chosen view is remembered between visits.

The best route is the dashboard's global Search page, /search?q=<name>&scope=products. It renders a real, accessible table. Each result is a role=row, and its cells are links to /products/<id>. - nameInput = this.generalInformation.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Name" }). It is the input name="name" and has no own test id. Scope it to the card, because other "Name"-like fields exist on the page.

- open(name): goto /search?q=<encodeURIComponent(name)>&scope=products. Wait for searchResultRow.filter({ hasText: name }) to have count 1, then click its name link. The seed's default scenario has no E2E Hoodie, so I explored with populatedb's "Hoodie", reached through /search?q=Hoodie&scope=products. Validation of an empty name, renaming from the variant page, and product-list display of the new name. They could be separate stories later. The ticket asks for one user story.

1	# Products: staff can rename a product (ticket 07)
2	
3	## Application Overview
4	
5	Covers ticket tickets/07.md. An admin opens the product "E2E Hoodie" from the orders scenario, renames it to "E2E Zip Hoodie", and saves with the savebar's Save button. The new name shows in the page header right away and is still there after a reload, which proves it persisted.
6	
7	## Setup, following CLAUDE.md "E2E conventions" and e2e/README.md
8	
9	- Spec file: e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts. It opens with a comment saying what it covers and why: there is no product-page coverage yet, and a rename that silently fails to save is the kind of failure nobody notices.
10	- Import test and expect from "../../fixtures/test.ts", never from @playwright/test. Relative imports keep the .ts extension.
11	- Use test.use({ scenario: ORDERS_SCENARIO }). ORDERS_SCENARIO and PRODUCTS are imported from "../../scenarios/orders.ts". The original name is PRODUCTS.hoodie.name ("E2E Hoodie"). The new name is a spec constant: const NEW_NAME = "E2E Zip Hoodie".
12	- Actor: the default admin, so the spec needs no actor override and no UI sign-in.
13	- No new scenario, no API set-up, no beforeEach or afterEach, no cleanup, no unique or timestamped names. The fixture restores the database before every test. Do not tag the test parallel(), because it writes.
14	- No hard-coded product ids, since ids change with every dump build. The test reaches the product through the UI by name (see "Reaching the product" below).
15	- Title is a sentence ending in the #e2e tag, for example "staff can rename a product and the new name persists #e2e". An area tag such as #products may follow it.
16	- One test with three test.step stages: "open the product", "rename and save", "reload and verify". Mark the set-up with // Arrange. Mark the steps // Act & Assert, because acting and asserting alternate stage by stage.
17	- No waitForTimeout and no networkidle. Do not change retries or timeouts. Assertions are web-first, for example await expect(locator).toHaveValue(...).
18	
19	## Reaching the product (no stable id)
20	
21	The Products list (/products) is a Glide data grid drawn on a canvas. Its rows are not real DOM rows or links, and the only way into them is the legacy fiber hack (clickGridCell in e2e-legacy/pages/basePage.ts). Do not use it. The tile view (tile-view-button) does have DOM tiles, but each tile's test id contains the product id (product-tile-<id>), and the chosen view is remembered between visits.
22	
23	The best route is the dashboard's global Search page, /search?q=<name>&scope=products. It renders a real, accessible table. Each result is a role=row, and its cells are links to /products/<id>. The search index for the scenario's products is filled at seed time by lib/beat.ts (update_products_search_vector_task). That is the same index the draft-order product picker relies on in draft-pricing.spec.ts.
24	
25	The search is full-text, so the query "E2E Hoodie" can also return populatedb's own "Hoodie". Narrow the rows with .filter({ hasText: PRODUCTS.hoodie.name }) and wait for exactly one row before clicking, in the same way as DraftOrderPage.addProduct.
26	
27	## Locators verified in the running dashboard (stable target, :9200)
28	
29	New page object e2e/pages/productPage.ts, class ProductPage. Locators are readonly fields initialised from this.page, with constructor(readonly page: Page) {}. Nothing in e2e/pages/ covers products today: the folder has addressDialog, draftOrderPage, homePage, loginPage and orderPage only.
30	
31	Search page (/search):
32	- searchInput = page.getByTestId("search-input"). The search box (role textbox, name "Search") also uses data-test-id search-input inside list-search-field. It is only needed if the test types the query instead of navigating to the query URL.
33	- searchResultRow = page.getByRole("row"). There are no data-test-ids on src/search. Use .filter({ hasText: name }) to narrow it. Each row has three links (type, name with category, date) and all three point to the product URL. Click the link that holds the name: row.getByRole("link").filter({ hasText: name }).
34	
35	Product details page (/products/<id>):
36	- pageHeader = page.getByTestId("page-header"). This is the top bar. Its text is the product name plus the product type (for example "Hoodie" then "Sweatshirt"), so do not assert toHaveText on the whole header.
37	- Page title (product name in the header): pageHeader.getByText(name, { exact: true }). The name lives in a Box with title={product.name} (src/products/components/ProductUpdatePage/Title.tsx), which has no test id. Expose a method or getter that takes the name, for example title(name). Optional, out of scope for this test-only ticket: adding data-test-id="product-details-title" to that Box would allow toHaveText. The loading skeleton is data-test-id product-details-title-skeleton.
38	- Browser tab title: the document title also follows the name ("Hoodie | Saleor e-commerce" became "Zip Hoodie | Saleor e-commerce" after saving). It can be checked with expect(page).toHaveTitle(new RegExp(`^${NEW_NAME} \|`)) as a supporting assertion.
39	- generalInformation = page.getByTestId("product-general-settings"). This is the General Information card.
40	- nameInput = this.generalInformation.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Name" }). It is the input name="name" and has no own test id. Scope it to the card, because other "Name"-like fields exist on the page.
41	- saveButton = page.getByTestId("button-bar-confirm"). This is the savebar Save button. It is disabled while the form is clean, enabled once the name is edited, and disabled again after a successful save (the form is clean again). It carries data-test-state (default, loading, success). The savebar Back button is button-bar-cancel.
42	- Save-success signal: the toast "Product updated" (from src/products/views/ProductUpdate/handlers/useProductUpdateHandler.ts). Locate it as page.getByRole("region", { name: /Notifications/ }).getByText("Product updated"). The toast element carries data-test-type="success" but no data-test-id. After the toast, the Save button returning to disabled proves the form took the saved value.
43	- Other ids seen in the header that the test does not need: app-header-back-button, product-type-display, show-product-metadata, show-more-button. The page form is product-update-form.
44	
45	Suggested ProductPage methods (named for the user's action, with a why-comment where needed):
46	- open(name): goto /search?q=<encodeURIComponent(name)>&scope=products. Wait for searchResultRow.filter({ hasText: name }) to have count 1, then click its name link. Wait for nameInput toHaveValue(name). Comment: the product list is a canvas grid with no clickable rows, and ids differ per dump, so the global search is the route.
47	- rename(name): nameInput.fill(name), then saveButton.click(). Then wait for the "Product updated" toast and expect saveButton toBeDisabled. Comment: Save is also disabled before any edit, so the toast is what proves this save landed, and the disabled state that follows proves the form took the saved value.
48	
49	## Checked during exploration
50	
51	The seed's default scenario has no E2E Hoodie, so I explored with populatedb's "Hoodie", reached through /search?q=Hoodie&scope=products. Renaming it and clicking Save showed the "Product updated" toast. The header and the tab title changed to the new name at once, and Save became disabled. After page.reload(), the Name input and the header both showed the new name. The test itself must use the orders scenario and PRODUCTS.hoodie.name.
52	
53	## Out of scope for this ticket
54	
55	Validation of an empty name, renaming from the variant page, and product-list display of the new name. They could be separate stories later. The ticket asks for one user story.
56	
57	## Test Scenarios
58	
59	### 1. Products: rename
60	
61	**Seed:** `e2e/tests/seed.spec.ts`
62	
63	#### 1.1. staff can rename a product and the new name persists #e2e

71	    - expect: The URL is a product details page (/products/...)
72	    - expect: The General Information Name input (getByTestId('product-general-settings') > textbox 'Name') has the value 'E2E Hoodie'
